from.place: Proof paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient adjunction and inverse-limit calculation: coherent homotopy-colimit foundation used by small-diagram rectification. Technical input: Finite direct diagrams in a Brown localization. Subargument: Brown localization over a fibrant base and lifting of slice sections.

title: Brown localization over a fibrant base
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category with a terminal object $1$ and classes $W,F$ containing all isomorphisms and closed under composition. Assume $W$ has two-out-of-three and is retract closed, every $X\to1$ lies in $F$, pullbacks of members of $F$ along arbitrary arrows exist and lie in $F$, pullbacks of members of $F\cap W$ lie in $F\cap W$, and every arrow factors as a member of $W$ followed by a member of $F$. Call members of $F\cap W$ trivial fibrations. These are the all-fibrant Brown hypotheses; no model structure or functorial factorizations are assumed. Use the quasicategories, mapping spaces, coherent diagrams and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], enlarging universes to contain all categories in question. A localization $q:N\mathcal C\to L\mathcal C$ means the universal functor on entire coherent functor categories inverting $W$.

For $b\in\mathcal C$, the ordinary slice $\mathcal C/b$ has arrows to $b$ as objects and commuting triangles over $b$ as morphisms. Let $\mathcal C(b)$ be its full subcategory on fibrations to $b$, with fibrations and weak equivalences detected in $\mathcal C$. For a quasicategory $\mathcal D$ and vertex $d$, the coherent slice $\mathcal D_{/d}$ has as its $n$-simplices maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal D$ with last vertex $d$; operators are restriction along the ordinal maps extended to preserve the new last vertex. In particular its edges retain their triangle homotopies. The category $\mathcal C(b)$ satisfies the all-fibrant Brown hypotheses, and the functor induced by $q$ on these slices is an equivalence
$$L(\mathcal C(b))\simeq (L\mathcal C)_{/qb}.$$
In particular, for a fibration $t:T\to P$ and a specified coherent section $h:qP\to qT$ of $q(t)$, including its triangle homotopy over $qP$, there exist a trivial fibration $s:Z\to P$ and an arrow $a:Z\to T$ with $ta=s$ exactly, whose localized fraction represents that section up to homotopy in the slice over $qP$.

source.place: Theorem 7.5.18 and Corollary 7.6.13 (fibrant slice localization); the section clause read with the trivial-fibration fractions of Corollary 7.2.18, formula (7.2.10.4) and Brown Lemma 7.4.13 applied in the slice. No Stacks tag states this coherent slice calculus. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archived source in literature/.

proof.text: Put $T=F\cap W$. Products exist by pulling back maps to $1$, and their projections lie in $F$. For any $f:X\to Y$, factor its graph as $X\xrightarrow{i}H\xrightarrow{r}X\times Y$, with $i\in W$ and $r\in F$. Set $d=\operatorname{pr}_Xr$ and $e=\operatorname{pr}_Yr$. Then $di=1_X$, $ei=f$, and $d,e\in F$. Two-out-of-three gives $d\in T$; if $f\in W$, it also gives $e\in T$. Thus every weak equivalence has the split factorization required by the fraction-model theorem, without functorial choices.

For any $b$, the terminal object of $\mathcal C(b)$ is $1_b$, and the map from $(X,p)$ to it is $p\in F$. Underlying pullbacks of fibrations stay in this full slice: the structure map of the pullback is a composite of fibrations. The same holds for trivial fibrations. To factor $f:(X,p)\to(Y,r)$, factor $f=v w$ in $\mathcal C$, and give the intermediate object the structure map $rv$; it is in $F$. Composition, two-out-of-three and the retract closure of $W$ are inherited on underlying maps. These verify every Brown hypothesis for $\mathcal C(b)$, so the graph argument of Step 1 applies there too.

Apply [lem-coef-trivial-fibration-fraction-model] to $\mathcal C$ and to every $\mathcal C(b)$, using Steps 1-2. In each case $T$ contains isomorphisms and is closed under composition and arbitrary pullback, by the given hypotheses; Step 1 supplies the required split weak-equivalence factorizations. Obtain essentially surjective localizations with the entire coherent-functor-category universal property. Write $R(x,y)$ for its fraction category of spans $x\xleftarrow{s}v\xrightarrow{a}y$, $s\in T$, with arbitrary commuting apex maps. Its nerve models $\operatorname{Map}_{L\mathcal C}(qx,qy)$, naturally under target maps and relative functors. A different localization specified in the question is equivalent to this one by applying its universal property in both directions; the two composite functors restrict to the identity, and full faithfulness of restriction supplies the coherent inverse equivalences. We may therefore use this model for $q$.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories

proof.text: If $v:b'\to b$ is any arrow, pullback gives $v^*:\mathcal C(b)\to\mathcal C(b')$ preserving underlying trivial fibrations. For a weak equivalence $f$ in $\mathcal C(b)$, the graph construction there gives $f=e i$, $di=1$, with $d,e$ trivial fibrations. After pullback, $v^*d,v^*e\in W$, and $(v^*d)(v^*i)=1$ implies $v^*i\in W$; hence $v^*f\in W$. This proves preservation of weak equivalences between fibrations over a fixed base directly from the axioms.

source.place: Corollary 7.4.14 and Proposition 7.4.15, graph argument written out

proof.text: We need right properness on underlying arrows. First suppose $j:b'\to b$ is a section of $d:b\to b'$ in $T$, and let $p:E\to b$ be in $F$. Form $E_0=b\times_{b'}E$, where $E\to b'$ is $dp$. The projection $d_0:E_0\to E$ is in $T$, the other projection $r_0:E_0\to b$ is in $F$, and $i=(p,1_E):E\to E_0$ satisfies $d_0i=1_E$. Thus $i\in W$ and is an arrow of $\mathcal C(b)$. Step 4 makes $j^*i$ a weak equivalence. The identity $dj=1$ identifies $j^*E_0=b'\times_b E_0$ with $E$ by $(b',b,e)\mapsto e$, with inverse $e\mapsto(dp(e),jdp(e),e)$. Under this identification $j^*i$ is the projection $b'\times_b E\to E$, which is therefore in $W$.

source.place: Proposition 7.4.16, section case of right properness

proof.text: For an arbitrary $v:b'\to b$ in $W$, Step 1 gives $v=e i$ with $e:H\to b$ and $d:H\to b'$ in $T$, and $di=1$. If $p:E\to b$ is in $F$, then $E_H=H\times_b E\to E$ is in $T$ and $E_H\to H$ is in $F$. Step 5 applied to the section $i$ gives $b'\times_H E_H\to E_H$ in $W$. Its composite with $E_H\to E$ is the projection $b'\times_b E\to E$ under the iterated-pullback isomorphism. Hence this projection is in $W$. This establishes right properness without a saturation or model-structure assumption.

source.place: Proposition 7.4.16, reduction using Brown graph factorization

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] to identify the join slice $D_{/d}$ with the fixed-target arrow slice, and apply [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] with singleton shape. For $p:x\to d$ and $r:y\to d$ this gives, naturally, $\operatorname{Map}_{D_{/d}}(p,r)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_p(\operatorname{Map}_D(x,y)\xrightarrow{r\circ-}\operatorname{Map}_D(x,d))$. An arrow of this slice whose underlying arrow is an equivalence is itself an equivalence: for each testing object postcomposition is an equivalence on ambient mapping spaces (compose with an inverse and the two inverse homotopies), with identity on the base mapping space. [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] then gives equivalences on the displayed fibers. Surjectivity on components at the target yields a right inverse in the slice; injectivity at the source gives the other inverse equation. [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] turns these inverse equations into equivalence edges. This argument also proves that such an underlying equivalence reflects correctly with its triangle homotopy.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories

proof.text: The simplicial map on join slices induced by $q$ restricts to $N\mathcal C(b)\to(L\mathcal C)_{/qb}$; a simplex of an ordinary slice is exactly a chain followed by its structure map to $b$. An underlying $W$-arrow is sent to an equivalence in $L\mathcal C$, so Step 7 shows its slice image is an equivalence. The coherent universal property in [lem-coef-trivial-fibration-fraction-model] therefore gives the comparison $G_b:L\mathcal C(b)\to(L\mathcal C)_{/qb}$. It remains to prove it fully faithful and essentially surjective; no slice comparison has yet been assumed.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories

proof.text: Fix fibrations $p:x\to b$, $r:y\to b$, and let $U:R(x,y)\to R(x,b)$ postcompose the right leg with $r$. For $a=(s:u\to x,c:u\to b)$ in $R(x,b)$ put $y_a=u\times_b y$ with structure map $s\operatorname{pr}_u:y_a\to x$, a fibration. An object of $(U\downarrow a)$ consists of $(t:v\to x,g:v\to y)$ and $h:v\to u$ with $sh=t$, $ch=rg$. The pair $(h,g)$ is uniquely an arrow $v\to y_a$ over $x$. This identifies $(U\downarrow a)$ with the fraction category from $1_x$ to $(y_a,s\operatorname{pr}_u)$ in $\mathcal C(x)$. On morphisms both categories require an apex map $k:v\to v'$ with $t'k=t$, $g'k=g$, $h'k=h$; the last two equations are exactly equality after the two pullback projections. Thus the identification is an isomorphism of categories, and Step 3 identifies its nerve with the corresponding localized slice mapping space.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories

proof.text: For a morphism $a_0\to a_1$ of $R(x,b)$ with underlying $h:u_0\to u_1$, the equation $s_1h=s_0$ and $s_0,s_1\in T$ give $h\in W$. Its induced map $h_y:y_{a_0}\to y_{a_1}$ is a pullback of $h$ along the fibration $y_{a_1}\to u_1$, so belongs to $W$ by Step 6. It is an arrow of $\mathcal C(x)$ and is inverted there. Under Step 9, the comma transition is precisely postcomposition by $h_y$. The naturality clause of [lem-coef-trivial-fibration-fraction-model] and composition with an inverse to the image of $h_y$ prove that $N(U\downarrow a_0)\to N(U\downarrow a_1)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This verifies every transition hypothesis needed for Quillen B.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories

proof.text: Take $a_p=(1_x,p)$ in $\mathcal B=R(x,b)$ and let $V:\mathcal B_{/a_p}\to\mathcal B$ be the domain projection. It is a discrete fibration: the unique lift of $\beta:a'\to a$ with specified target $(a,\gamma:a\to a_p)$ has source $(a',\gamma\beta)$. Its domain has terminal object $(a_p,1)$, and the unique arrows into this object give a natural transformation from its identity functor to the constant functor there. [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] contracts its nerve. The strict pullback $R(x,y)\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B_{/a_p}$ is exactly $(U\downarrow a_p)$. Apply [lem-coef-quillen-b-discrete-fibration-base-change], using Step 10. It identifies $N(U\downarrow a_p)$ with the homotopy fiber over $a_p$ of $NR(x,y)\to NR(x,b)$. The comparison retains the path supplied by the comma arrow, as it is induced by the strict pullback square and the contraction just specified.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories

proof.text: At $a_p=(1_x,p)$ the comma condition of Step 9 forces $h=t$, and its remaining equation is $pt=rg$. Consequently $(U\downarrow a_p)$ is exactly the fraction category in $\mathcal C(b)$ from $(x,p)$ to $(y,r)$: $v$ has structure map $pt\in F$, $t\in T$, and $g$ is over $b$. Its morphisms are precisely the same commuting apex maps. The fraction models, their coherent naturality under target maps, and Step 11 now give $\operatorname{Map}_{L\mathcal C(b)}(p,r)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{qp}(\operatorname{Map}_{L\mathcal C}(qx,qy)\to\operatorname{Map}_{L\mathcal C}(qx,qb))$. Here $a_p$ maps to $qp$, and a commuting fraction maps to its fraction together with the triangle over $qb$. Thus, by Step 7, this is the map on mapping spaces induced by $G_b$, not merely an abstract equivalence of the two spaces. [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] justifies passage through the equivalences of total and base fraction spaces. Since every source object is equivalent to an ordinary slice object by Step 3, precomposition and postcomposition with these equivalences extend the result to all source objects. Hence $G_b$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories

proof.text: For an arbitrary slice object $\alpha:z\to qb$, choose an equivalence $e:qx\to z$ by the essential surjectivity of [lem-coef-trivial-fibration-fraction-model]. Its fraction clause gives $s:u\to x$ in $T$ and $f:u\to b$ with a path from $qf(qs)^{-1}$ to $\alpha e$ in the mapping space. Equivalently this supplies a triangle $qf\simeq\alpha e\,qs$. Factor $f=r w$, with $w:u\to y$ in $W$ and $r:y\to b$ in $F$. In the target slice, the object $qf:qu\to qb$ maps both to $\alpha:z\to qb$ by $e\,qs$ with the specified triangle, and to $qr:qy\to qb$ by $qw$ with its strict triangle. Both underlying arrows are equivalences; Step 7 makes both slice arrows equivalences. Thus $\alpha$ is equivalent to $G_b(y,r)$, proving essential surjectivity, including for objects $z$ not originally in the image of $q$.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to the fully faithful $G_b$ of Step 12. Step 13 says its full essential image is the whole target slice. That node supplies a coherent quasi-inverse and coherent natural inverse equivalences. This proves the claimed equivalence of quasicategories, with its prescribed comparison functor.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories

proof.text: Finally take $b=P$. The objects $1_P$ and $t:T\to P$ lie in $\mathcal C(P)$ since $t\in F$. Regard the specified section, with its given triangle homotopy, as a point of the mapping space from $q1_P$ to $qt$ in the target slice. Full faithfulness of $G_P$ lifts its component to $\operatorname{Map}_{L\mathcal C(P)}(1_P,t)$. Apply [lem-coef-trivial-fibration-fraction-model] inside $\mathcal C(P)$: it represents this component by $1_P\xleftarrow{s}(Z,z)\xrightarrow{a}(T,t)$, with underlying $s\in F\cap W$. Being over $P$ means $z=s$ and $ta=z=s$ exactly. Its fraction maps to the originally specified component in the slice mapping space; the resulting homotopy is in that space, so includes the prescribed triangle homotopy rather than merely the equation $[qt][h]=1$ in the ordinary homotopy category.

source.place: Corollary 7.6.13; explicit fraction-space proof for ordinary Brown categories
